program.name: ndm_hipass
program.help:
High-pass filter a .dat file (required for spike extraction).
PARAMETERS
# filter
butterworth (default when unset) or median. butterworth runs a zero-phase Butterworth high-pass (process_butterworth): forward then backward, no phase distortion, -6 dB at the corner, effective order 2 x order, linear. median is the historical median-subtraction high-pass (process_medianfilter), which is non-linear: its output is exactly 0 wherever the centre sample is the window median, and it adds broadband content the .dat does not have.
# highPassHz
butterworth: high-pass corner in Hz (default 800).
# lowPassHz
butterworth: optional low-pass corner in Hz (default 0 = none).
# order
butterworth: design order (default 3; 6 after zero phase).
# precision
butterworth: auto (default; double on the CPU, single on a GPU), double or single.
# windowHalfLength
median: half-length of the median window in samples; 16 at 32.5 kHz gives an effective -3 dB corner of about 800 Hz.
# chunkSize
median: number of bytes of input processed per pass (default 134217728 = 128 MiB). Reduce it if memory is tight. Capped internally at 512 MiB, so a larger value is clamped rather than honoured.
# inputExtension
Extension of the data file read for filtering, without the leading dot (default dat). Point it at an alternative, externally-processed source (e.g. car.dat) to filter that file instead of the raw recording.
